content: 1. The prevention of chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis was discussed in a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1989, volume 320, issue 12, pages 769-772. 2. Hammershlag MR and colleagues conducted a study on the use of erythromycin ointment for ocular prophylaxis of neonatal chlamydial infection, published in JAMA in 1980, volume 244, issue 20, pages 2291-2293. 3. Hammershlag MR and colleagues also performed longitudinal studies on chlamydial infections during the first year of life, published in Pediatric Infectious Disease in 1982, volume 1, issue 6, pages 395-401. 4. Isenberg SJ and colleagues proposed a double-application approach for the prophylaxis of ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology in 2003, volume 87, issue 12, pages 1449-1452. 5. Isenberg SJ, Apt L, and Wood M conducted a controlled trial on the use of povidone-iodine as prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1995, volume 332, issue 9, pages 562-566. 6. Laga M and colleagues compared the efficacy of silver nitrate and tetracycline for the prophylaxis of gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1988, volume 318, issue 11, pages 653-657. 7. Matinzadeh ZK and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of topical ophthalmic prophylaxis in preventing ophthalmia neonatorum, published in Tropical Doctor in 2007, volume 37, issue 1, pages 47-49. 8. Ozkan H and colleagues conducted a controlled trial on the efficacy and safety of povidone-iodine for prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Child Health and Diseases in 1999, volume 42, issue 4, pages 459-467 (in Turkish). 9. Ramirez-Ortiz MA and colleagues studied the use of 5% povidone-iodine eye drops and ophthalmic chloramphenicol for preventing neonatal conjunctivitis in a trachoma-endemic area in southern Mexico, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology in 2007, volume 91, issue 11, pages 1430-1434. 10. Steigleder GK examined the effectiveness of neonatal ocular prophylactic treatment for preventing chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis, published in Z Hautkr in 1989, volume 64, issue 5, page 347 (in German). 11. Zanoni D, Isenberg SJ, and Apt L compared silver nitrate with erythromycin for prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum, published in Clinical Pediatrics in 1992, volume 31, issue 5, pages 295-298. 12. Knapp JS and colleagues reported on the frequency and distribution of Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains with plasmid-mediated, high-level resistance to tetracycline in the United States, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1987, volume 155, issue 4, pages 819-822. 13. Ison CA and colleagues documented tetracycline-resistant gonococci in the UK, published in The Lancet in 1988, volume 1, issue 8586, pages 651-652. 14. Isenberg SJ, Apt L, and Wood M conducted a controlled trial on povidone-iodine as prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 15. Schwarcz SK and colleagues described the national surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae through the Gonococcal Isolate Surveillance Project, published in JAMA in 1990, volume 264, issue 11, pages 1413-1417. 16. Hedberg K and colleagues reported an outbreak of erythromycin-resistant staphylococcal conjunctivitis in a newborn nursery, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 1990, volume 9, issue 4, pages 268-273. 17. Deogan CL and colleagues performed a cost-effectiveness analysis of the Chlamydia Monday community-based intervention to reduce chlamydia prevalence in Sweden, published in the Scandinavian Journal of Public Health in 2010, volume 38, issue 2, pages 141-150. 18. Keenan JD, Eckert S, and Rutar T analyzed the cost of povidone-iodine for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in Archives of Ophthalmology in 2010, volume 128, issue 1, pages 136-137. 19. The International Drug Price Indicator Guide (2014 edition) provided additional cost-related references, accessed on June 6, 2016. 20. Kakar S and colleagues identified Chlamydia trachomatis as a cause of neonatal conjunctivitis in a tertiary care center, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Microbiology in 2010, volume 28, issue 1, pages 45-47. 21. Darling EK and McDonald H conducted a meta-analysis on the efficacy of ocular prophylactic agents for preventing gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health in 2010, volume 55, issue 4, pages 319-327.
